quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What does a DOT-approved helmet do?

options.text: Reduces the severity of head injuries.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the severity of head injuries.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet greatly reduces your risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. It does not limit your side vision.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Nothing if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face, not just your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace a face shield.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the left arm is extended straight out to the left, it signals a left turn or lane change to the left. Hand signals work instead of or with your turn signals.

questions.question: What sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: How should you help drivers merging from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move to another lane if you can.
Do nothing—they are responsible for merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Merging drivers may not see your motorcycle. Give them room to merge safely by moving to another lane if possible.

questions.question: How fast should you ride at night?

options.text: The same speed as during the day.
On the road shoulder so others can see you.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day under the same conditions. Darkness makes it harder to see hazards, and slower speeds help you avoid accidents.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction and crash.

questions.question: What should you NOT do on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Never brake suddenly.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?
questions.explanation: Oregon law has mandatory severe penalties for riding under the influence. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, just minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before starting to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs tell drivers the rules of the road. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when turning and riding curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast can:

options.text: Cause the rider to drift into another lane.
Be better than going too slowly.
Usually keep the rider in their lane.
Be acceptable because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause the rider to drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before turning or taking a curve.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to follow you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.
All three portions as the vehicle passes.

questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Staying on the far side may cause the driver to turn back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Passing on a motorcycle is similar to passing in a car. However:

options.text: Being seen is more important for a motorcycle.
Being seen is less important for a motorcycle.
Pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being seen is more important for a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Being seen is more critical on a motorcycle than in a car. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily hide in a car's blind spot. Drivers may not see you even when looking.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, the group should:

options.text: Let them go ahead and meet at a designated spot later.
Speed up to keep everyone together.
Split up so everyone rides at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them go ahead and meet at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If a rider wants to go faster, let them go ahead and arrange to meet at a planned location later.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around your motorcycle before moving.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help lower the chance of a crash?

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Let them know your plans through clear signals and lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch for hazards ahead. Do not rely on hoping drivers will see you.

questions.question: What is the best way to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times at intersections. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see it clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can react if danger appears. Do not assume eye contact alone will make drivers notice you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. Instead, hold the handlebars tight without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and down as much as possible. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: A motorcycle that fits properly allows you to:

options.text: Touch the ground with your feet while seated.
Have the seat at your waist level.
Have the seat 10 inches above your waist.
Have the seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet when you sit on it. When riding, keep your feet on the footrests.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear hearing protection:

options.text: At all times to protect their hearing.
Never, because it blocks horns and sirens.
Never, if they wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times to protect their hearing.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear earplugs or other hearing protection. You will still be able to hear important sounds like horns and sirens.
